title: 18 — Design Maps and Navigation (Google Maps)
html:
18 — Design Maps and Navigation (Google Maps)

The one idea: three separate systems share a map. Rendering serves precomputed image/vector tiles at many zoom levels from a CDN. Location updates stream in at huge volume and feed traffic estimates. Navigation runs shortest-path search over a road graph split into hierarchical routing tiles, so a cross-country route never loads every side street.

Step 1 — Scope

  • 1 billion DAU; features: location update, navigation (with ETA), map rendering.
  • Accuracy matters (wrong directions are unacceptable); smooth rendering; low data and battery usage.

Map 101

  • Positioning: latitude/longitude; the Earth is projected onto a flat map (Web Mercator).
  • Tiles: the world is split into 256×256 px tiles; zoom level z has 4^z tiles. Clients fetch only the tiles in view.
  • Road data as a graph: intersections = nodes, roads = edges; weights = travel time.
  • Geocoding: address ↔ lat/lng.

Estimates

  • Tiles: zoom 21 ≈ 4.4 trillion tiles × ~100 KB ≈ 440 PB — but ~90% is ocean/empty and compresses to almost nothing → realistically ~50–100 PB for all zoom levels.
  • Location updates: 1B users × 35 min of navigation/week ≈ 5B navigation-minutes/day. Batched every 15 s → 4 requests/min → 20B requests/day ÷ 10^5 ≈ 200,000 QPS, peak ~1M.

Step 2 — High-level design

---
title: Maps and navigation — high-level architecture
---
flowchart TB
    C["Client"] -->|"location batches"| LS["Location service"]
    LS --> Kafka["Kafka / stream"]
    LS --> LDB[("User location DB")]
    Kafka --> Traffic["Traffic update service"]
    Kafka --> ML["ML: personalisation, road changes"]
    C -->|"route request"| NS["Navigation service"]
    NS --> GC["Geocoding service"]
    NS --> RP["Route planner"]
    RP --> SP["Shortest-path service"] --> RT[("Routing tiles<br/>object storage")]
    RP --> ETA["ETA service"] --> TDB[("Traffic DB")]
    RP --> RK["Ranker + filters<br/>(no tolls, no highways)"]
    C -->|"tile URLs"| CDN["CDN"] --> TS[("Precomputed map tiles")]

Location service

  • Clients batch location points (e.g. every 15 s) → far fewer requests.
  • Write-heavy, time-ordered → Cassandra-style store keyed by (user_id, timestamp).
  • Also published to Kafka for traffic, ML, and road-change detection.

Map rendering

  • Tiles are precomputed per zoom level and served as static files from a CDN — cache-friendly and scalable.
  • Client computes the tile URL from (lat, lng, zoom) → often via a geohash-like key; or asks a small service for the tile URL set.
  • Vector tiles (paths/polygons) instead of raster images: smaller, crisp at any zoom, smooth zoom transitions.

Step 3 — Deep dive

3.1 Routing tiles

The road graph for the planet is too big for one in-memory search. Split it into routing tiles (a grid, geohash-based), each holding its nodes/edges plus references to neighbouring tiles. Load tiles on demand as the search expands.

Hierarchy (three levels):

Level Contents Tile size
Local All roads Small
Arterial Arterial roads between districts Medium
Highway Highways between cities Large

Long routes search the local level near origin/destination and the highway level in between — like contraction hierarchies.

3.2 Shortest path

  • A* / Dijkstra over routing tiles, fetched from object storage and cached in memory.
  • Results are top-k candidate routes, not one.

3.3 ETA

Current traffic + historical patterns → ML prediction of travel time per edge. Hard part: predicting traffic 10–20 min ahead.

3.4 Ranker

Apply user filters (avoid tolls/highways), rank by ETA, return the top route and alternatives.

3.5 Adaptive ETA and rerouting

Track active navigating users per routing tile; when traffic changes on a tile, recompute ETAs for users whose route crosses it and push updates (WebSocket). Maintaining "users per tile" at scale is the tricky part — index by tile at a coarse level.

3.6 Delivery protocols

WebSocket for pushing reroutes/ETA changes to navigating clients; plain HTTP + CDN for tiles.

Step 4 — Wrap-up

Add multi-stop routing, "conditional" routing (depart at time X), public transport. The core ideas: CDN-served tiles, batched location streams into Kafka, hierarchical routing tiles, and ML-driven ETA.

.NET / Azure mapping

  • Azure Maps provides render (raster/vector tiles), route (with traffic), geocoding and spatial operations — build on it rather than recreating tiles in most real projects.
  • Location ingestion: Event Hubs (Kafka-compatible endpoint) → Stream Analytics or Azure Data Explorer for traffic aggregation.
  • Tiles: Blob Storage + Front Door; tile keys like /{z}/{x}/{y}.pbf.
  • Routing tiles cached per instance with IMemoryCache (size-limited) over Blob Storage.
  • Push reroutes: SignalR Service groups per routing tile.

Review checklist

  • Split into location updates, rendering, navigation.
  • Tiles + zoom levels + CDN; vector vs raster.
  • Batched location updates → stream.
  • Routing tiles with hierarchy; A*.
  • ETA from live + historical traffic; adaptive rerouting.
